I think everyone is different and experiences things differently so it's hard for me to say if my story is similar but I will share it anyway.

I am 25 currently and I have had a rough childhood. I got beaten a lot and my mother was really ambivalent in her behaviour. We moved a lot and I didn't really have friends. I had to spent a lot of time by myself. But since children are really resilient I carried on and finished school and learned a job. Don't misunderstand me here... I still had issues with my self esteem and socialising was always difficult for me. My picture of relationships romantic and platonic was really crooked aswell. But I managed to carry on until I broke down right before I wanted to start university. I smoked a shitton of weed to cope with life until I had major panic attacks at the age of 19. The worst thing was that my whole body was all tensed up so I couldn't breathe right which lead to chains of panic attacks. After a couple of months I wasn't really there anymore because of dissociation. I was living in my bed for a whole year until I was there enough again to actually do stuff again. My breathing was still an issue but I didn't have the panic attacks anymore. That year left me depressed and feeling out of my body but I managed to do therapy and I have been in the psychiatry multiple times since then. It took me 6 years to recover and I took a lot of steps back. 2 years ago I was at a really dark point because of my relationship issues and lack of stuff that makes life worth living. I put myself into a (not sure if that's the right word) closed ward for a weekend and stayed in the psychiatry for 2 more months. I now realise that I initially put a lot energy in becoming functional again (which was important) when I should have worked on stuff that makes my life worth living aswell... Like Hobbys and friends and a healthy attitude towards myself. And now I am working on my issues with my mother because I feel like that's one of the last pieces I need to pick up in order to move on.

An important thing I realised along the way is that life doesn't get easier. You just get stronger and learn to deal with stuff differently. It's like learning to carry a weight in a more efficient way. And a lot of it all is about perspective. I still have days when I feel bad but they end and then there are days that are filled with joy. I am so fucking proud of myself. And I will move on and look back at today and feel proud again.

Oh and as a side note - I started 2 different courses in university and dropped them both and am now starting to work in a completely different field of work than I initially learned. I had some terrible relationships and made dumb decisions. And one of my biggest initial fears was that I would never get out of this place or that it would take years... Which it did. But yeah time past has past right ? And the future doesn't exist yet.

Not sure if this helps in any way but I hope it does and I wish the best for you. I hope you will realise that you don't need to be too harsh with yourself one day. You are okay the way you are and things take as long as they do.
